title: Surf Tech RuneScape: Dragonwilds
author: Abendix
description: I found a way to take no fall damage by surfing in Dragonwilds!

transcript.text: Today I want to talk about an interesting mechanic in Dragon Wilds, surfing. Normally when you use wind
stepping, it reduces gravity and slows down your fall, which in turn reduces fall damage. However, you can still take
damage and from certain heights, you can even die. But there's a trick. If you fall onto a steep enough surface, like
the side of a cliff, it can significantly reduce the damage you take. In fact, if the slope is at just the
right angle, it can completely negate the damage. This means it's possible to jump
from great heights and surf down cliffs to safely land even without using windstep. Most steep cliffs won't fully
prevent fall damage without windstep, but they can still greatly reduce it. A simple way to check if a slope is
good for surfing is to stand on it. If you automatically slide down, then it's steep enough to surf
on. While experimenting with this mechanic, I got the idea that it might be useful for speedrunning the crystal
ball quest since the quest starts on top of a high cliff. However, it turns out that Archie had already discovered and
used this trick in a speedrun. Here's the spot he found. While looking for more usable
natural ramps, I wondered, could you build structures for surfing, too? And it turns out you can. Using Ashocks, you
can build 60° angled beams. These beams are so steep that you automatically slide down them, making them perfect for
surfing. While exploring, I also find a natural spot, a pet surrounded on all sides by steep enough slopes, allowing
you to fall into it without taking damage. However, escaping from the pit does require wind
step. That gave me another idea. What if you put opposite facing 60° beams close
together? This way you could safely fall between them and climb out without needing wind step. And it turns out this
works. Finally, I took it a step further and combined multiple rams. The end result is this.
Buildable surf ramps enable you to jump from anywhere and place a ramp under yourself midfall to avoid most fall
damage. It's a bit tricky to pull off and it can't negate the damage completely. So often it's more practical
to pre-place ramps in useful spots. Leggings of lightness are not as good as windstep, but you can combine
them together resulting in very little to no damage taken from most heights.
Thank you for watching and see you next time.
